newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-GOOCH FAVOURITE TO TAKE OVER AS ENGLAND SUPREMO.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-GOOCH FAVOURITE TO TAKE OVER AS ENGLAND SUPREMO.

text.p: Graham Gooch became favourite to take over as chairman of the England selectors when he hinted on Friday he would be prepared to end his lengthy playing career to take up the post.

The 43-year-old former England captain still has a year of his contract to run at Essex but an almost certain condition of him taking on the job vacated by Ray Illingworth would be for him to quit playing.
Said Gooch: "I am contracted to play for Essex next season but I would have to give the matter serious thought if I was approached to be England's chairman.

"However, I don't think it is possible to be both a player and serve as chairman. Other than that there is not much else I can say on the topic, except that I believe David Graveney would make a very good chairman."

Graveney's route to the high-profile position was effectively blocked by the Professional Cricketers' Association (PCA) who felt there would be a conflict of interests as the former Gloucestershire captain is secretary of their organisation.
